alt: Curved field lines leave the N pole and enter the S pole of a bar magnet, crowded together at the poles and spreading out further away. Two plotting compasses line up with the field, their N ends pointing along the arrows. A list gives the rules for drawing field lines.
caption: Field lines run from N to S, never cross, and crowd together where the field is strong.

alt: Two flat magnets placed parallel with a north face above a south face. In the central part of the gap the field lines are straight, parallel and equally spaced, pointing from N to S; near the edges they bulge outwards.
caption: Opposite flat poles facing across a small gap give a uniform field in the middle.

after: ## Forces between magnets and magnetic substances
alt: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic; copper, aluminium, brass, wood, plastic and glass are not. A test bar repelled by either pole of a known magnet is a magnet. A steel bar attracted to both ends is not, because the magnet induces an unlike pole in its nearer end.
caption: A magnet attracts unmagnetised iron too, so only repulsion proves a magnet.
